style: Calm-premium dark product demo for NestRoutine, a baby-routine app. One continuous vertical 'breath' on deep navy: nothing slams, every element rises/settles on the same slow easing family. A single phone holds real app screenshots while iOS-style push notifications drop onto it, stacked one after another — the notifications ARE the story, so they own the frame for most of the runtime. Appeal: tired new/expecting parents — gentle, quiet, reassuring. No narration, no cuts, no store badge, no URL. All copy in English.

brief: A phone breathes up out of deep navy holding the NestRoutine Home screen. Before any copy is legible, the first real push notification drops onto it: 'Nap time!' — 'Baby may need to sleep in 15 minutes' — and the screen beneath cross-fades to the Sleep tracker, so you see where the reminder leads. That card lifts away and the second signature alert drops into the same slot in warm amber: 'Sleep window closing!' — 'Baby may get overtired. Put baby down now.' While it holds, the three things the app tracks arrive as coloured chips under the phone — Sleep (lavender), Feeding (terracotta), Diaper (teal) — each one swapping a real screenshot into the phone as it lands. The cards lift, everything settles, and the app icon + wordmark resolve over the line 'Never miss the sleep window.' One dominant motion idea: every element enters with the same slow rise-and-settle (or drop-and-settle) easing, so drop-in, cross-fade, chips and lockup read as one continuous exhale rather than five separate animations.
